# v1.1.0-dev.83 — The display editor stops scrolling, and stops shouting

Pre-release off the `dev` branch. Builds on `v1.1.0-dev.82`.

Five things, all in the display editor, all of them things you can see.

## It Doesn't Scroll Any More

The editor's body overflowed by four pixels. Not enough to hide anything,
exactly enough to put a scrollbar down the side of a dialog that should
have fit.

Those four pixels were the hint line under the monitor picker wrapping onto
a second row. Shortening it took the whole panel back under the line, with
room to spare.

## The Hint Under The Picker

It used to read "Select a display to change its settings. Drag one to move
it, or hold Shift and press an arrow key.", which was long enough to wrap,
and it shared its row with the arrangement chip and its button.

The first half is something the picker teaches by itself the first moment
you click a monitor. The part worth the space is the keyboard route, which
nothing else tells you about. That is what stayed:

> Drag a monitor to move it, or **Shift** + arrows.

The key is drawn as a key. The full sentence is still there if you hover
it.

## The Buttons Along The Bottom

Six of them, all the same weight, all shoulder to shoulder, and each one
taller than it needed to be.

They are shorter now. More usefully, the three on the left are secondary
actions: removing the display step, opening the history, opening another
editor. They are drawn as plain text rather than as three more buttons, so
the row reads as three quiet actions and three real ones instead of six of
a kind.

## The Options Sit In A Box Now

Scaling, Orientation, Resolution and Refresh rate were laid out across the
full width of the dialog, with the "now 2560 × 1440" readout on a stretchy
column. Every pixel the window gained went into empty space to the right of
it. The wider the window got, the further the controls drifted from their
own labels.

They live in a fixed-width box now, centred, still left aligned inside. The
monitor's name travels with it. Widen the window and the group stays put
instead of pulling apart. As a side effect the editor opens noticeably
narrower, because it no longer needs the width it was never using.

## Resolutions Stop Calling Themselves Portrait

Two things were wrong on a rotated display.

Every resolution group was labelled "(portrait)": "16:9 (portrait)", "3:2
(portrait)", and so on down the list. That label exists to separate
stood-up sizes from wide ones inside a single list. Windows reports every
mode in the display's current orientation. On a display that is already
rotated it therefore landed on every group at once and told you nothing.
It now appears only when a list genuinely holds both shapes.

The largest size on offer was tagged "(native)". It isn't. That tag was
going on the biggest mode the driver reports, which is not the same thing
as the panel's own resolution. Windows never reports the latter here. A
2560 × 1440 virtual display offers 4096 × 2160. The editor was therefore
calling your monitor something it is not. It says "(largest)" now, which is true.

Two related reports could not be reproduced on this build: a landscape
monitor whose orientation read "Portrait", and a trip through portrait and
back leaving the sizes flipped. Both check out clean here, including a full
round trip that restores the size list and every group label exactly. The
likely explanation is the freeze that dev.82 fixed. Until then the editor
was being buried under thousands of duplicate display-changed events per
change. An editor re-seeding itself mid-flood would look precisely like
that. If you still see either on this build, it is a different problem and
worth saying so.

## Install

Auto-updates from dev.53 and later. Otherwise unzip and run.
